title.narrative: Emergency Multi-Sector Rohingya Crisis Response Project

description.narrative: The Emergency Multi-Sector Rohingya Response Project of Bangladesh has the proposed development objective to strengthen the Government of Bangladesh systems to improve access to basic services and build faster and social resilience of the displaced Rohingya population. This project is comprised of four components: (1) Strengthening delivery of basic services, resilient infrastructure, emergency response and gender-based violence (GBV) prevention. (2) Strengthening community resilience. (3) Strengthening institutional systems to enhance service provision to the displaced Rohingya population. (4) Contingent emergency response component.
To strengthen the Government of Bangladesh systems to improve access to basic services and build the disaster and social resilience of the population of Cox's Bazar district.

condition.narrative: Institutional Arrangements (FA Section I.A and I.B of Schedule 2). By no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, theRecipient shall establish and maintain throughout the implementation period of the Project (a) two (2) Project steering committees;(b) through the implementing agencies, such number of Project Implementation Committees within each of these implementing agencies;and (c) through the implementing agencies, such number of Project Implementation Units within each of these implementing agencies,each with a mandate, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association.For purposes of implementing Part 2 of theProject, the Recipient through MoDMR shall maintain, throughout the period of implementation of the Project, the Refugee Relief andRepatriation Commissioner's office and the camps in charge (CiCs), with functions and resources satisfactory to theAssociation.Project Operations Manual (FA Section I.B of Schedule 2.) The Recipient for implementing Part 2 of the Project shallcarry out the Project in accordance with the Project Operations Manual in a manner satisfactory to the Association. Sub-projects(FA Section I.B of Schedule 2) . The Recipient through MoDMR shall ensure that only those Community Services Subprojects andCommunity Workfare Subprojects selected, prepared and implemented in accordance with the requirements set out in the ProjectOperational Manual, ESMF, shall be financed out of the proceeds of the Financing, including those related to the selection of thedisplaced Rohingya population and the associated provision of Stipends or Wages, as applicable, for carrying out said subprojects.Agreements with UN Agencies/NGOs (FA Section I.E of Schedule 2). The Recipient shall enter into appropriate standard formof agreement(s) between the Recipient and the UN Agency(ies) and/or NGOs approved by the Association when entering into a contractwith any UN Agency or NGO .Safeguards (FA Section I.C of Schedule 2). The Recipient shall ensure and cause each of theImplementing Agencies to ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance with the provisions of the ESMF, the RPF and allSafeguard Assessments and Plans and the requirements of the Grievance Redress Mechanism. To this end, the Recipient shall ensurethat the appropriate review, clearance and public disclosure of all Safeguard Assessments and Plans as required by the ESMF and theRPF.
Section 1. F , Schedule 2. The Recipient shall ensure that the Project excludes any activities related to repatriation orrelocation of displaced Rohingya population.

Section III.C, Schedule 2. In the event that the Association has determined that any amounts allocated for Stipends and Wages to beprovided to beneficiaries under Part 2 of the Project have not reached the beneficiaries in accordance with the requirements of theProject Operational Manual, the Recipient shall, promptly upon notice from the Association, refund such amounts to the Association.

title.narrative: Number of people with access to improved public infrastructure as a result of the project

comment.narrative: Number of people with access to at least one basic service as a result of this project: street lights, lightning protection, connectivity, water and sanitation, or local markets. Access to lightning protection system in the camps and roads in the host community are considered as they cover the greatest number of beneficiaries. So far, 825 lightning protection systems installed inside the camps that cover 757,254 DRP. 296.4 km roads constructed as access roads in the vicinity of the camps and in host community areas that benefit around 312,754 people (total 296.4 km roads improved under the project, of which 15.9 km roads are inside the camps and 280.5 km are access roads to the camps and host community roads. People located within half km on each side of the roads are considered as beneficiary host community. For calculation, population density of respective Upazillas is considered as per Census 2011).

title.narrative: Beneficiaries directly reached by communication activities as a result of the project

comment.narrative: 757,254.23 DRP are covered by lightning protection systems installed in different camps and 404,000 host community are reached by communication activities, as reported by LGED. The consulting firm BCCP has completed all key deliverables under the contract, covering outreach activities in both the host communities and in DRP camps. The key outreach activities included street drama, a 4-episode community radio program, miking program & courtyard meetings, sermons and orientation for Imams (religious leaders), Sessions with children on WASH practice, children's sports and painting competition, demonstrations on LPG gas use, production of signboards, video, posters, leaflets, pictorial booklets, calendars, and capacity building training among others. Since the last mission, nota activities have included video production, a social media campaign, media outreach, women's group meetings, coordination meetings with CIC officials and Upazila level stakeholders, and orientation of field staff.

title.narrative: Households participating in community workfare and services

comment.narrative: Number of eligible households participating in workfare and services activities. 37. An array of activities was supported through community services and workfare. Community services included volunteer services, awareness training and monthly conditional food assistance transfers. Skills development trainings on masonry, carpentry, and plumbing were also organized for youth DRPs. Community workfare included three groups of works: site improvement and disaster risk reduction (e.g., drainage canals improvement), accessibility maintenance and improvement (e.g., rehabilitation of access roads and footpaths), and environmental protection (e.g., plantation of indigenous trees). A camp-based implementation committee (CBIC) oversaw activities in each camp. Workfare schemes identified through the Site Development and Site Management agencies, DRP communities and Camp-in-Charges (CiCs) were confirmed in monthly CBIC meetings.

title.narrative: Women and girls using GBV services as a result of the project

comment.narrative: As a result of the project, 24,000 women and girls from the DRP camps and host community are using GBV services. A to of 16 WFS were operationalized in 13 camp locations and 3 host communities. The project reached 652,899 beneficiarie (418,639 female and 234,260 male) through the community mobilization interventions till June 2023. Around 244,776 women and girls visited the EMCRP supported facilities (18 WFS and 4 Health facilities) out of which 237,906 women and girls visited the 16 facilities newly established under the project.. The contract with UNFPA completed and ended on September 30, 2023.

title.narrative: Development of the DRP Camp Management System

comment.narrative: The project strengthened CiCs governance and DRP engagement capacity as well as fostered community participation through enhancement of the Rohingya volunteer network. The project ensured participation of CiCs in all programme related processes and enhanced logistics support for improved coordination, planning and management of multiagency activities in the camps. Furthermore, trainings were arranged on grievance management, community engagement, disaster management, public procurement and financial management and gender mainstreaming, for participants from the line ministry, RRRC office including CiCs, PIUs and other relevant officials. Moreover, five types of GRM are in place for MoDMR part - (i) a WFP toll-free hotline that directly records all complaints; (ii) site management "info hubs" and information centers; (iii) onsite feedback and complaints collections and cooperation partners; (iv) WFP helpdesk; and (v) Rohingya food-security committee gathers and reports general comments.

Moreover, five types of GRM are in place for MoDMR part - (i) a WFP toll-free hotline that directly records all complaints; (ii) site management "info hubs" and information centers; (iii) onsite feedback and complaints collections and cooperation partners; (iv) WFP helpdesk; and (v) Rohingya food-security committee gathers and reports general comments.

title.narrative: People provided with at least basic water

comment.narrative: Number of people with access to one of the following: mini piped water schemes, deep tube well, or mobile water treatment plant. Liters/person/day: In post-emergency refugee situations, the minimum allocation of water is 20 liters p person per day. This standard covers domestic and individual needs only. Coverage means dwellings no further than 200 from water points up to the maximum design standard (no more than 100 people per water point). 1982 tap stands and 700 deep tube wells in the camps and; 11370 household connections of piped water, 1930 community water options and 200 Rainwater harvesting systems in the host community have been constructed which make the total beneficiary 437,985 in the camps and the host community.
